title: Cramer's Rule OQ-05-OQ-01: Similarity is an Equivalence Relation, Preserved by Polynomial Evaluation
description: Answers the first open question of cramers-rule-oq-05: matrix similarity IsSimilar M N := ∃ U, N = U M U⁻¹ over a commutative ring is a genuine equivalence relation (symmetry by conjugating with U⁻¹, transitivity by the product unit V·U), bundled as a Setoid, and is preserved by polynomial evaluation p(M) ~ p(N). The conceptual mechanism is that conjugation by a unit is not just a ring map but an R-algebra automorphism conjAlgEquiv U, so evaluation commutes with it (Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply); this yields power-invariance M^k ~ N^k and equal characteristic polynomials for p(M), p(N) as corollaries. 7 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 axioms.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. Fully machine-verified. Depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
originalContributions: IsSimilar.symm and IsSimilar.trans: similarity is symmetric (conjugate back by U⁻¹) and transitive (conjugate by the product unit V·U)
isSimilar_equivalence / isSimilarSetoid: the bundled Equivalence and Setoid making 'similarity class' well defined over an arbitrary commutative ring
conjAlgEquiv: conjugation A ↦ U A U⁻¹ by a unit packaged as an R-algebra automorphism of the matrix ring, the structural reason similarity is preserved by every polynomial expression

IsSimilar.aeval: similar matrices have similar polynomial evaluations p(M) ~ p(N) via the same unit, with corollaries IsSimilar.pow (M^k ~ N^k) and IsSimilar.charpoly_aeval (equal charpoly of p(M), p(N))

overview.historicalContext: Similarity of matrices — N = U M U⁻¹ for an invertible U — is the matrix shadow of representing the same endomorphism in two different bases, a viewpoint that crystallized in the 19th-century invariant theory of Cayley, Sylvester, and Frobenius. That similarity is an equivalence relation is what makes the notion of a 'similarity class' (and hence canonical forms such as the rational and Jordan forms) well posed. The stronger observation formalized here — that a change of basis is an algebra automorphism, so it carries along not just the matrix but every polynomial expression in it — is the conceptual engine behind the fact that the whole commutative subalgebra R[M] generated by a matrix, including its minimal and characteristic polynomials, is a basis-independent invariant of the underlying operator.
overview.problemStatement: Building on cramers-rule-oq-05, which defined IsSimilar M N := ∃ U, N = U M U⁻¹ and proved only reflexivity: show that similarity is a full equivalence relation (symmetry and transitivity), bundle it as a Setoid, and prove it is preserved by polynomial evaluation, i.e. M ~ N implies p(M) ~ p(N) for every polynomial p.
overview.text: Over a commutative ring R and a finite index type n, two matrices M, N ∈ Matrix n n R are similar when N = U M U⁻¹ for a unit U ∈ (Matrix n n R)ˣ. Symmetry follows by conjugating back by U⁻¹, and transitivity by conjugating with the product unit V·U (using (V·U)⁻¹ = U⁻¹·V⁻¹). Together with the parent's reflexivity these make IsSimilar an equivalence relation, packaged as a Setoid. The preservation statement is proved by recognizing that A ↦ U A U⁻¹ is an R-algebra automorphism conjAlgEquiv U of Matrix n n R: it preserves products, sums, and scalars. Because polynomial evaluation commutes with any algebra homomorphism (Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply), applying conjAlgEquiv U to p(M) yields p(U M U⁻¹) = p(N), so p(M) ~ p(N) via the same unit U. Specializing p = X^k gives M^k ~ N^k, and composing with the parent's charpoly invariance gives equal characteristic polynomials for p(M) and p(N).
overview.proofStrategy: Part I: IsSimilar.symm destructures the witness and conjugates back by U⁻¹ using U⁻¹ U = 1; IsSimilar.trans conjugates by V·U, reducing (V·U)⁻¹ via mul_inv_rev in the unit group; isSimilar_equivalence bundles refl/symm/trans and isSimilarSetoid packages the Setoid. Part II: define conjAlgEquiv U as an AlgEquiv with the four structure obligations (left/right inverse, map_mul', map_add', commutes') discharged by matrix associativity and U U⁻¹ = 1; conjAlgEquiv_apply certifies it agrees definitionally with the parent's conj U. Part III: IsSimilar.aeval reduces to Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply for conjAlgEquiv U; IsSimilar.pow specializes to X^k via aeval_X_pow, and IsSimilar.charpoly_aeval composes with the parent's IsSimilar.charpoly_eq.
keyInsights: Everything holds over an arbitrary commutative ring R, not just a field — conjugation by a *unit* matrix suffices, so the equivalence relation and preservation results apply over ℤ and polynomial rings

The right abstraction is not 'conjugation is a ring map' but 'conjugation is an R-algebra automorphism' — packaging it as conjAlgEquiv U is exactly what lets polynomial evaluation slide through, giving preservation for every polynomial expression at once rather than one fixed quantity

Preservation by aeval is strictly stronger than invariance of any single quantity such as determinant or trace: it carries the entire subalgebra R[M] along the change of basis, so p(M) and p(N) are themselves similar (not merely equal in some invariant)
Transitivity hinges on the unit-group identity (V·U)⁻¹ = U⁻¹·V⁻¹, mirroring how composing two changes of basis composes their transition matrices

The structural upgrade is free: conjAlgEquiv_apply, which certifies that the new AlgEquiv agrees with the parent's bare function conj U, is proved by rfl. Packaging conjugation as an algebra automorphism adds no computational content and requires no new definition of 'what conjugation does' — it only proves that the already-existing function happens to preserve the full algebra structure, which is precisely what unlocks aeval_algHom_apply.

R-algebra automorphisms (AlgEquiv) of the matrix algebra

conclusion.summary: Fully machine-verified: matrix similarity over a commutative ring is an equivalence relation (bundled as a Setoid) and is preserved by polynomial evaluation, p(M) ~ p(N), via the algebra automorphism conjAlgEquiv realizing conjugation by a unit. Corollaries: M^k ~ N^k and equal characteristic polynomials for p(M), p(N). Zero axioms, zero sorries.
conclusion.implications: Making IsSimilar a genuine equivalence relation legitimizes the notion of a similarity class, the foundation for canonical-form theory (rational and Jordan forms) and for treating invariants as functions on classes rather than on representatives. The algebra-automorphism packaging makes precise that a change of basis is an isomorphism of the full operator algebra, so any construction natural in the matrix — powers, polynomials, the minimal polynomial, the generated commutative subalgebra — is automatically a similarity invariant. This is the natural launching point for formalizing that the minimal polynomial is a similarity invariant and that similar matrices share rank and eigenvalue data.
openQuestions: Show the minimal polynomial is a similarity invariant by transporting minpoly along conjAlgEquiv (minpoly.algEquiv_eq), completing the pair with the parent's characteristic-polynomial invariance
Prove the quotient Matrix n n R / isSimilarSetoid carries the induced invariant maps det, trace, charpoly as well-defined functions on similarity classes
Extend preservation from single polynomials to the whole generated subalgebra: conjAlgEquiv restricts to an isomorphism R[M] ≅ R[N] of commutative subalgebras
